GPN.thesis_one_line: A newly combined card-payments processor trading at about six times adjusted profit, but its cash flow and a cut forecast are not yet proven.
kill_criteria: Consolidated net debt (10-Q Note 6 "Total long-term debt" less balance-sheet cash and cash equivalents) divided by adjusted EBITDA above 3.75x at any quarter-end.
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance cut below $13.60 or normalized constant-currency adjusted net revenue growth guided below 4%.
Normalized adjusted net revenue growth below 3% for two consecutive quarters.
Operating cash flow minus capital expenditures (consolidated cash flow statement) for calendar 2026 below $1.5bn.
Worldpay run-rate expense synergy target of $600m by year-end 2028 reduced or delayed.
key_adverse_facts: FY26 adjusted EPS guide cut on 5 Aug 2026 from $13.80-$14.00 to $13.60-$13.80 (Middle East travel)
H1'26 operating cash flow $374m; TTM OCF less capex about $0.8bn
Income taxes payable $2,450m at 30 Jun 2026 vs $118m at 31 Dec 2025, timing not explained in the 10-Q
GAAP net loss attributable H1'26 $(1,787)m; GAAP-to-adjusted EPS gap $3.41 in Q2
Total long-term debt $22,418m consolidated; interest about $1bn a year; covenant 4.50x
data_conflicts: Triage cited net debt/EBITDA of about 4x; my estimate is about 2.9x (about 3.3x after the tax payable); Worldpay purchase accounting provisional
Normalized FCF ($2.0-2.5bn) is my estimate; reported TTM is about $0.8bn
GPN.confidence_in_thesis: low: cash conversion and the tax liability are unverified in the filings

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for GPN. Reverse DCF implies FCF -0.4% to -3.5% a year on $2.0-2.5bn normalized FCF versus my +5% base, but +11.7% on reported TTM FCF, so the call depends on cash conversion.

GPN.scenario_basis: Start adjusted EPS $13.70 (guide midpoint); growth -2%/+7%/+12%; exit 5.5x/7.0x/9.0x adjusted EPS; dividend $1.00 a year.

KMI.thesis_one_line: America's largest natural-gas pipeline owner with a record year and 3.9% dividend yield, but the price already assumes more growth than it can show.
kill_criteria: Company-defined Net Debt-to-Adjusted EBITDA above 4.0x at any quarter-end (now 3.6x).
FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA finishing below the $8.6bn budget.
Natural gas transport volume growth below +3% year on year for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26: +7%).
Dividend growth below 2% or any cut to the $0.2975 quarterly dividend.
key_adverse_facts: Q1'26 beat was helped by winter storm Fern and cold weather; Q2 adj. EBITDA $2,199m vs Q1 $2,539m
Total debt $32,144m consolidated; net debt/adjusted EBITDA 3.6x company-defined
Project backlog fell to $9.6bn from $10.1bn as projects entered service
2026 budget implied only +2.5% adjusted EBITDA growth; about 20x adjusted EPS
Products Pipelines volumes -5% and crude -16% in Q2'26
data_conflicts: Triage said forward EPS growth is flat; guidance now implies about +17% adjusted EPS in 2026 (at least 12% above $1.36 budget)
Q1'25 and Q2'25 adjusted EPS derived from stated growth percentages, not stated directly
KMI.confidence_in_thesis: medium: business quality high, valuation the constraint

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for KMI. Reverse DCF implies 5.2% a year FCF growth for 10 years at 8% cost of equity versus my 3.5% base; price near $27 would equal base.

KMI.scenario_basis: Start adjusted EPS $1.52 (budget $1.36 plus 12%); growth 0%/4%/6%; exit 16x/19x/21.5x; dividend $1.19 growing 2% a year.

WAT.thesis_one_line: A leading maker of lab analysis instruments, raising its forecast all year after buying BD's biosciences unit, but priced for near-flawless growth.
kill_criteria: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance cut below $14.30 (the February low end).
Organic constant-currency revenue growth below 4% for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26: 9%).
Revenue of the acquired Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions businesses shrinking year on year on a comparable basis in any quarter (Q2'26: +4%).

Consolidated net debt (debt-note "Total debt" less balance-sheet cash) above $4.5bn at fiscal year-end 2026 (4 Jul 2026: $5,086m less $539m = $4.55bn). [DV43 2026-10-09: already exceeded at the as-of date; threshold needs resetting, e.g. $5.0bn]
Company-defined adjusted free cash flow for 2H26 below $500m (H1: $161m).
key_adverse_facts: Q2'26 adjusted EPS grew only 3% (dilution from 98.2m vs 59.7m shares and FX); GAAP net loss $(136)m
H1'26 adjusted FCF $161m vs $392m in H1'25; about 60% of FY EPS falls in H2
Goodwill and intangibles about 72% of $24.8bn assets; deferred-close businesses in China and Italy still legally held by BD
Head of Analytical Sciences Division resigned 17 Aug 2026 (8-K 21 Aug 2026)
data_conflicts: Triage flagged leverage risk; my estimate is about 2.2x net debt/EBITDA (Waters does not publish it)
Normalized FCF $1.35bn is my estimate (reported adjusted FCF H1 $161m)
WAT.confidence_in_thesis: medium: franchise strong, valuation and integration cash flow unproven

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for WAT. Reverse DCF implies 9.7% a year FCF growth at 8.5% cost of equity versus my 8% base; price near $380 would equal base. [DV43 2026-10-09: start FCF $1.35bn assumed 95% conversion of adjusted net income; FY2025 conversion was 69% and SBC is not deducted; on about $1.0bn FCF after SBC implied is 13.6-17% a year and the equal-to-base price is about $222-281; implied_vs_base stays above]

WAT.scenario_basis: Start adjusted EPS $14.55 (guide midpoint); growth 4%/10%/13%; exit 22x/27x/31x adjusted EPS; no dividend.
